overview: Prospective observational study of all adults entering the pharmacist-led tapering pathway at Vellmoor General Hospital from November 2026 to October 2027, each followed for 12 months with outcomes collected at the existing fortnightly calls and 6 and 12 month clinic visits.
population: Adults aged 18 or over on long-term opioid therapy of 50 mg oral morphine equivalents a day or more for at least three months who choose to taper and enter the pathway; about 85 expected over 12 months. Patients whose opioids are prescribed for opioid use disorder are managed by another service and are not included.
exposure: The pathway as delivered: written taper plan agreed with the physician, pharmacist call every two weeks, naloxone kit and same-week review for withdrawal or pain flares. Pace is agreed with each patient and never exceeds 10 percent of the daily dose per month; the study adds no dose target, deadline or reminder.
procedures: At entry the pharmacist records daily dose, pain interference (0 to 10), the eight-item telephone withdrawal checklist, distance from the clinic, interpreter need and a depression screen. At each fortnightly call the pharmacist records dose and the checklist. At 6 and 12 months the clinic visit records pain interference, and dose is confirmed from the dispensing history. Patients who stop answering calls receive one letter; with consent given at entry, their dispensing history and hospital attendances are still collected so that dose and emergency visits are known after they leave.

outcomes.name: Percent change in daily opioid dose
outcomes.measure: Daily oral morphine equivalent dose from the dispensing history at 6 months minus entry dose, divided by entry dose
outcomes.why: Continuous, comparable across patients and not a target; the proportion reaching 25 percent is reported only descriptively.

outcomes.name: Pain interference with daily life
outcomes.measure: 0 to 10 rating of interference with daily activities
outcomes.why: The outcome patients care about most while tapering.

outcomes.name: Emergency visits or admissions for withdrawal, uncontrolled pain or overdose
outcomes.measure: Count per participant from hospital data and patient report
outcomes.why: A pathway that lowers dose must not raise acute harm.

feasibility: About seven entries a month give about 85 participants in 12 months. Data collection uses calls the pharmacist already makes, adding about five minutes per call for the checklist; dispensing and hospital data are extracted twice by the pharmacist.
biasMitigation: Primary outcome from dispensing history, available even for patients who leave
Written definitions of disengagement and of each emergency visit category fixed before the first entry
Analysis plan registered before data collection starts
Outcomes reported separately for patients living more than 60 km away and for those needing an interpreter

biasFlags.label: Loss of patients who leave
biasFlags.note: Mitigated by consent to dispensing and hospital data at entry.

biasFlags.label: No concurrent comparison
biasFlags.note: Findings describe pathway patients; no causal claim.

biasFlags.label: Self-selection into tapering
biasFlags.note: Participants chose to taper; results do not transfer to patients who did not.

flags: Disengagement model limited to two predictors
parsimony.simplestPath: One clinic, one year of entries, outcomes from existing calls and dispensing data.

theoreticalFramework: No behavioural framework is used; a pre-specified causal diagram guides the disengagement analysis.
summary: Prospective follow-up of about 85 participants with a continuous dose outcome, patient-reported secondary outcomes and safety outcomes for everyone, including those who leave.
